newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA TATAS TIE-UP WITH SINGAPORE'S EASTGATE.
newsitem.headline: INDIA TATAS TIE-UP WITH SINGAPORE'S EASTGATE.

text.p: BOMBAY, Aug 8 (Reuter) _ India's largest business house, the Tatas, has tied up with the Singapore-based Eastgate Holdings Pvt Ltd., to set up $8-million facilities to make compact disks, in India, the group said in a statement.
"The proposed joint venture which involves an investment of around $8 million will in the next three years have an installed manufacturing capacity of 30 million CDs per annum," the statement said.

"Tata Exports Ltd and Tata Precision Industries (India) Ltd.(TPIL), have entered into a memorandum of understanding with Eastgate Holdings for setting up in India a facility for manufacture of CD-ROMS, audio compact disks, video CDs and other related products for the domestic market as well as exports," the statement added.
The joint venture, combining the strengths of the three promoters, is expected to become a market leader in the country, the statement said.
The manufacturing facilities are scheduled to be set up at Dewas in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh, where TPIL, is located.

Eastgate Group has diversified interests in multi-media products, compact disk manufacturing and electronics manufacturing, the statement said. It has manufacturing facilities in Singapore, China, Japan, Hong Kong and Malaysia.
"This joint plant will be the fourth manufacturing unit of Eastgate," it said.
TPIL manufactures high-precision machined components for electronics and other sophisticated industries, the statement said.
